title: Theo's Nightlight Rules
status: concept-proposal (Creative Director, 2026-11-19; not approved; awaiting owner review)
hook_line: Theo has three rules about his nightlight.
first_visual: A moth-shaped nightlight in a dark child's room; on the wall, faint shadows all facing it.

beats.visual: The moth nightlight glows; faint shadows on the wall all face it.
beats.vo: Theo has three rules about his nightlight.

beats.visual: Theo in bed counts on his fingers to Ivy.
The nightlight flickers; Theo grabs Ivy's face to make her look at him.
beats.vo: 'Two: if it flickers, look at me. Not it.'

beats.visual: The nightlight dies; darkness; Theo's small hand catches Ivy's at the switch.
beats.vo: 'Three: if it goes out, never turn on the big light.'
I'm the grown-up. I turned it on.

beats.visual: Key moment: the room is packed with tall thin figures shoulder to shoulder, all facing the dead nightlight.
beats.vo: They were all facing the nightlight. Like moths.

beats.visual: In the bright light every head turns from the lamp to Ivy.
beats.vo: It wasn't for Theo. It kept them looking at it.

beats.visual: Theo whispers; black; the moth nightlight flickers back on.

ending: Theo: 'Now they'll look at you.' Black. The moth nightlight flickers back on.
loop_note: Yes. It ends on the nightlight flickering back on, which is frame 1. On a rewatch, the wall shadows in frame 1 are the figures.

originality_review: Original rule-set that sets up the strongest brand inversion: the light protects by attracting. No 'goodnight' or parent-repetition device, so it does not follow the Lullorin structure. It avoids the porch-light/door premise.
scores_basis: Initial editorial judgement, 2026-11-19. topic_demand is an estimate linked to research/WEEKLY_TREND_REPORT.md categories, not a measurement of this concept.
concept: Theo's rules: keep the nightlight on; if it flickers, look at him, not it; if it dies, never turn on the big light. Ivy turns it on and sees the room packed with tall figures facing the dead nightlight like moths. It was never for Theo. It kept them looking at it.
